R.T: The current Labamu WMS supports batch, cluster and wave picking strategies on the back‑end and has
a workflow engine that can orchestrate put‑away and pick operations via specialised handlers.
However, the front‑end only exposes a single‑order picking session, and the Routes module still defines
simple one‑step "pull" rules without a graphical way to configure multi‑step sequences. The backlog
also notes that waveless (continuous‑flow) picking is planned but not yet implemented. This gap means
warehouse managers cannot take advantage of advanced fulfilment strategies such as batch/cluster/
wave picking, QC inspection or staging steps during inbound and outbound workflows, or dynamic
routing that adapts to real‑time conditions.
This PRD defines the functionality required to expose advanced picking strategies and multi‑step
workflows in the Labamu WMS UI, and to implement waveless continuous flow picking. By closing this
gap, operations teams will be able to configure and execute complex fulfilment scenarios – such as
wave picking with consolidation, QC inspection before put‑away, or staged packing – directly from the
user interface. The goal is to ensure parity between the back‑end capabilities and the front‑end
experience, thereby improving productivity, reducing travel time and enabling dynamic re‑sequencing
